discussion_comments.comment_body: AFAICT, if PyNumber_Add(b, ...) fails, b would be NULL right? then the next PyNumber_Subtract would fail. I think we should properly check each intermediate operation (though I agree that it's unlikely to fail we still need to)
According to its docs, it is both forbidden and pointless to call Py_DECREF on NULL. Can this be changed to use Py_XDECREF in the Done section, and avoid duplicating all of this code?

I think this is a bug.

when the spec has no `origin` attribute, this would null-deref

repro (that you can turn into a regression test)

```
class Spec:
    name = "abc"

_imp.create_dynamic(Spec())
```

on main, this raises `AttributeError`, on this PR it segfaults. works with the suggested fix:

```suggestion
        info.filename = PyObject_GetAttr(spec, &_Py_ID(origin));
        if (info.filename == NULL) {
            goto error;
```
